The World Health Organization (WHO) said it convened the first meeting of an International Health Regulations (IHR) Emergency Committee on the Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak affecting the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda.

According to WHO’s published update, the committee reviewed the cross-border public-health risk and issued temporary recommendations intended to guide surveillance, coordination, and response measures.

Why this fits the science-health desk: the development is a live infectious-disease event with direct implications for outbreak management, health-system readiness, and international public-health coordination.

What to watch next: additional national situation updates from health ministries and WHO guidance on implementation of the temporary recommendations.
